thought.text: I can use the sqlcmd inside the SQL container itself.

reasoning_content:
No sqlcmd. Either install mssql-tools, or create the DB using a dotnet one-liner with the Microsoft.Data.SqlClient NuGet package. The easier option is: installing the mssql-tools18 repository. Or using the SQL container's /opt/mssql-tools18/bin/sqlcmd — this can be executed inside the container!

`docker exec mssql /opt/mssql-tools18/bin/sqlcmd -S localhost -U sa -P 'Strassen#2024' -C -Q "CREATE DATABASE Strassennamen"`

action.command: for i in $(seq 1 20); do if docker exec mssql /opt/mssql-tools18/bin/sqlcmd -S localhost -U sa -P 'Strassen#2024' -C -Q "SELECT 1" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "SQL ready"; break; fi; sleep 5; done; docker exec mssql /opt/mssql-tools18/bin/sqlcmd -S localhost -U sa -P 'Strassen#2024' -C -Q "IF DB_ID('Strassennamen') IS NULL CREATE DATABASE Strassennamen" -Q "SELECT name FROM sys.databases" | head -10

tool_call.name: terminal
